chapters.summary: Council staff welcomes attendees to the New York City Council hearing for the Committee on Women and Gender Equity and asks everyone to silence cell phones and electronic devices. Staff then tells the Chair the committee is ready to begin.
chapters.title: Council staff calls hearing to order and asks for device silence

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to today's New York City Council hearing for the Committee on Women and Gender Equity.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: This time we ask you to silence all cell phones and electronic devices to minimize disruptions throughout the hearing.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, we are ready to begin.

chapters.summary: Council Member Amanda C. Farías identifies herself as Chair of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity and welcomes attendees to the vote. She acknowledges Council Members Gutierrez, Shulman, and Aldebol for being present.
chapters.title: Chair Farías opens meeting and acknowledges present colleagues

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you so much and good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Amanda Farias, and I'm Chair of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Welcome to today's vote.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I'd like to acknowledge my colleagues who are present, Council Members Gutierrez, Shulman, Aldebol,

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you all for being here.

chapters.summary: Chair Farías states that the committee will consider two resolutions. She then moves to introduce the first item.
chapters.title: Chair Farías announces two resolutions before committee

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Today, the committee will be considering two resolutions.

chapters.summary: Chair Farías introduces Resolution 441, sponsored by herself, which declares November 25 as the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women in honor of the Mirabal sisters. She explains the resolution's symbolic purpose.
chapters.title: Resolution 441 introduced honoring Mirabal sisters

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: First up is Resolution No.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: 441, sponsored by myself, declaring November 25th as the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women in honor of the Mirabal sisters.

chapters.summary: Chair Farías notes that women's rights activists have observed November 25 as a day against gender-based violence since 1981. She cites the 2025 NYC Domestic Violence Fatality Review Committee finding that females are 57.4% of domestic violence homicide victims and 78.6% of intimate partner homicide victims, arguing the designation spotlights gender-based violence in the city.
chapters.title: Farías cites NYC domestic violence statistics behind Resolution 441

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Women's rights activists have observed November 25th as a day against gender-based violence since 1981.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: The International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women is observed annually to raise awareness about the pervasive issue of violence against women and girls and calls for governments, organizations, and individuals to take action against gender-based violence.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: In New York City, violence against women remains a critical safety issue with the 2025 New York City Domestic Violence Fatality Review Committee reporting that females account for the majority, 57.4% of all domestic violence homicide victims.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: And 78.6% of intimate partner homicide victims.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: By designating November 25th as the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women in New York City, it puts a spotlight on the prevalence of gender-based violence in the city and reaffirms the city's commitment to make

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: this place a safer place for all people.

chapters.summary: Chair Farías introduces Resolution 637, sponsored by Council Member Santosuosso and herself. The resolution calls on the New York State Legislature and Governor to require insurers to cover all lactation consultation and counseling services without restrictions and reimburse providers accordingly.
chapters.title: Resolution 637 introduced on lactation consultation insurance coverage

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: The committee will also be considering Resolution No.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: 637, sponsored by Councilmember Santos-Woso and myself, calling on the New York State Legislature to pass and the Governor to sign legislation requiring insurers to cover all lactation consultation

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: and counseling services without restrictions and reimburse providers accordingly.

chapters.summary: Chair Farías says research shows breastfeeding provides the best nutrition for most infants and that lactation consultants support parents with breastfeeding challenges. She identifies high out-of-pocket costs and confusing insurance coverage as top barriers, and says insurers like UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield, and Cigna have restricted billing by treating the birthing parent and baby as one patient or contracting with a single lactation provider organization.
chapters.title: Farías details barriers and insurer restrictions on lactation services

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Research shows that breastfeeding provides the best nutrition source for most infants.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Lactation consultants are trained professionals equipped to support parents with breastfeeding challenges.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Studies have shown that the top barriers for accessing lactation consultation services were high out-of-pocket expenses for consultation, visits, and confusing insurance coverage.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: In recent years, insurers like UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield, and Cigna Healthcare have restricted billing and payment for lactation services by treating the birthing parent and baby as one patient

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: or by contracting with a single lactation provider organization for all in-network care.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: State legislation requiring insurance carriers to pay lactation consultants for all the services they provide would recognize the importance of breastfeeding care and would enable parents who choose to breastfeed to have comprehensive support for the health of their infants and themselves.

chapters.summary: Chair Farías reads a statement from Resolution 637's lead sponsor, Council Member Santosuosso, thanking Chair Farías, the bill drafter, and the Speaker's Office. The statement says that despite decades of research on lactation consultation benefits, insurance companies are still not mandated to cover these services.
chapters.title: Chair reads lead sponsor statement from Council Member Santosuosso

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I will now read a statement from the resolution's lead sponsor, Councilmember Sanzuzoso.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I want to express my deep gratitude to Chair Farias for including Resolution 637 on the committee agenda today, and I want to give special thanks to the bill drafter and the Speaker's Office for allowing us to take

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: the lead on this critical piece of legislation.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Despite decades of research demonstrating the clear health benefits of lactation consultation for babies and their caregivers alike, insurance companies are still not mandated to cover these types of services.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: This resolution calls on the state government to rectify this situation and ensure that lactation consultation and counseling services are covered and reimbursed without restrictions.

chapters.summary: The statement read by Chair Farías says early breastfeeding difficulties often force people to stop without professional support, and that disparities are rooted in systemic racism. It cites the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services on board-certified lactation consultants and calls on the Governor and Legislature to pass legislation ensuring access without out-of-pocket costs.
chapters.title: Santosuosso statement urges state action on lactation coverage disparities

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Difficulties early

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: on often force people to discount breastfeeding many times without seeking professional advice or support.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Research suggests that many of the disparities are rooted in systemic racism, which further perpetuates health disparities later in life.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: The U.S.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Department of Health and Human Services has reaffirmed that international board certification lactation consultants and other professionals are equipped to help parents navigate their challenges with breastfeeding.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: This greatly improves the chance that families will reach their infant feeding goals.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Given the clear health benefits to children and caregivers, there is no reason that lactation consultation should not be covered by health insurance companies in the state of New York.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: This resolution calls on the governor and state legislature to draft and pass legislation that will ensure

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: All New Yorkers have access to these critical services without having to pay out of pocket.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you to all of my colleagues on the Women and Gender Equity Committee for taking the time to consider this essential piece of legislation.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: That's the end of her statement, and I thank Councilmember Santos-Wilso for providing it.

chapters.summary: Chair Farías thanks her staff, Dan Curtin and Josephine Karras, and committee staff Julia Goldsmith-Pinkham, Katie Salina, and Ali Stauffer for preparing the meeting. Seeing no other hands for statements, she tells the Clerk the committee is ready to begin the vote.
chapters.title: Chair Farías thanks staff and calls for the vote

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Finally, I would like to...

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: to thank my own staff, Dan Curtin and Josephine Karras, and the members of the Women and Gender Equity Committee staff, Senior Committee Counsel Julia Goldsmith-Pinkham, and Legislative Policy Analyst Katie Salina, and Financial Analyst Ali Stauffer, who worked to prepare this meeting.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Seeing no other hands for statements, Clerk, we are ready to begin the vote.

chapters.summary: Committee Clerk Ben Jacobs announces the roll-call vote for Resolution 441 and Resolution 637, noting both items are coupled. He calls Chair Farias and Council Members Gutierrez, Shulman, Aldebol, and Santos-Hoso, who vote aye.
chapters.title: Clerk Ben Jacobs conducts coupled roll call on Res 441 and 637

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ben Jacobs, Committee Clerk, City Council Committee on Women and Gender Equity.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: This is the roll call vote for Resolution 441 and 637.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Both items are coupled.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair Farias.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Aye, vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Gutierrez.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Aye, vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Congrats.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Shulman.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Aldable.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Aye, vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Santos-Hoso.

chapters.summary: The Clerk announces that all votes are in favor, none are negative, and there are no abstentions. Both coupled items are adopted.
chapters.title: Committee adopts Res 441 and Res 637 with all affirmative votes

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I vote in favor of the affirmative, none in the negative, and no abstentions.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: The items are adopted.

chapters.summary: Chair Farías thanks the Clerk. She then declares the hearing adjourned.
chapters.title: Chair Farías thanks clerk and adjourns hearing

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you, clerk.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: This hearing is now adjourned.

summary: The Committee on Women and Gender Equity held a hearing and vote on Res 0441-2026 recognizing November 25 as the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women in honor of the Mirabal sisters, and Res 0637-2026 urging New York State to require insurance coverage for lactation consultation and counseling.

Chair Amanda C. Farías presented both resolutions, summarized domestic violence statistics and lactation coverage barriers, and read a statement from lead sponsor Council Member Kayla Santosuosso on Res 0637.
The committee conducted a coupled roll-call vote; all members present voted aye, both resolutions were adopted, and the hearing was adjourned.
title: Committee on Women and Gender Equity
topic: Declaring November 25 as the “International day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women.”
